report.source_text: Exploration showed distended small bowel with no restriction signs at the deep inguinal ring. We then decided to proceed to a midline laparotomy. We found caecal volvulus with a coecum located in the midline and an important distention of small bowel which were located at the right side of the abdomen (Fig. 2). There was also an abnormal position of the duodenojejunal (D-J) flexure which is located to the right of the midline (normally to the left). The final diagnosis was therefore a caecal volvulus associated with an incomplete common mesentery.

clinician.final_diagnosis: caecal volvulus associated with an incomplete common mesentery
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old male with ESRD on hemodialysis presented with acute abdominal pain, vomiting, and distension evolving over 24 hours. Physical examination revealed a large irreductible right inguinal hernia and empty rectal bulb. CT imaging demonstrated an abnormal duodenojejunal flexure positioned to the right of the midline (indicative of incomplete common mesentery), a midline transverse caecum contacting the anterior abdominal wall, and small bowel distention with a transition zone at the deep inguinal ring. Exploratory laparotomy confirmed caecal volvulus with the caecum located in the midline and small bowel positioned on the right side of the abdomen, corroborating the incomplete common mesentery. Pathological examination revealed signs of chronic ileocolic ischemia consistent with volvulus-induced vascular compromise.
